subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 3: The Making of a Global World
central_question: How did long-distance trade, migration, technology, colonialism, war and international institutions create an increasingly interconnected but unequal global economy?
in_scope_units: The Pre-modern World: early trade, travel, migration, ideas and disease across regions
Silk Routes Link the World: trade and cultural exchange across Asia, Europe and northern Africa
Food Travels: crops, food habits and the movement of plants between continents
Conquest, Disease and Trade: European expansion, American silver, smallpox and the shift of world trade toward Europe
The Nineteenth Century (1815-1914): the linked flows of trade, labour and capital
A World Economy Takes Shape: Corn Laws, food imports, migration, settlement and global agriculture
Role of Technology: railways, steamships, telegraph and refrigerated shipping
Late nineteenth-century Colonialism: imperial conquest, the partition of Africa and loss of livelihoods
Rinderpest: cattle plague, African livelihoods and colonial labour control
Indentured Labour Migration from India: recruitment, coercion, plantation life and cultural fusion
Indian Entrepreneurs Abroad: bankers, traders and financing export agriculture
Indian Trade, Colonialism and the Global System: textile decline, raw material exports, trade surplus and home charges
The Inter-war Economy: the First World War, post-war crisis and mass production
The Great Depression and India: causes, global transmission and unequal effects
Rebuilding a World Economy: the post-war settlement, Bretton Woods, decolonisation, G-77 and the later phase of globalisation
banned_topics: A complete modern account of twenty-first-century digital globalisation
Detailed military history of the First and Second World Wars beyond their economic effects in this chapter
The full history of Indian nationalism, which belongs to Nationalism in India
The detailed history of factory production in Britain and India, which belongs to The Age of Industrialisation

known_pitfalls.claim: Globalisation began only in the late twentieth century.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter traces long histories of trade, migration, capital, cultural exchange and disease from the pre-modern world onward.

known_pitfalls.claim: European conquest of the Americas depended only on superior weapons.
known_pitfalls.correction: Smallpox and other germs, against which indigenous populations lacked immunity, were a decisive force in conquest.

known_pitfalls.claim: The nineteenth-century global economy benefited all participants equally.
known_pitfalls.correction: It combined growth, migration and technology with slavery, indenture, colonial conquest, loss of livelihoods and forced labour.

known_pitfalls.claim: The Great Depression was caused by one event alone.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter identifies interacting causes, including agricultural overproduction, falling prices, dependence on US loans, withdrawal of lending, bank failures and protectionist tariffs.

known_pitfalls.claim: The IMF and World Bank were initially designed mainly for newly independent developing countries.
known_pitfalls.correction: They were created for post-war stability and reconstruction in the industrial world and shifted greater attention to developing countries only later.

recommended_example_progression: Explain the pre-modern transfer of disease using Write in brief Q2.
Analyse the three economic flows using Discuss Q7.
Explain rinderpest and indentured labour using Write in brief Q3(b) and Discuss Q6.
Explain the causes and Indian effects of the Great Depression using Discuss Q8 and Write in brief Q3(d).
Explain Bretton Woods and G-77 using Write in brief Q5 and Discuss Q9.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with Write in brief questions 1-5, Discuss questions 6-9, and a project on gold and diamond mining in nineteenth-century South Africa.
